Earlier this year, WhatsApp launched parent-managed accounts for children under thirteen. Today, WhatsApp is further extending parental supervision features to teenage accounts, adding group activity notifications and imposing more restrictions on Meta AI. Details are as follows.

WhatsApp Expands Parental Supervision Options

Earlier this year, WhatsApp announced a series of new features aimed at giving parents greater control over accounts for children under thirteen.

These features include allowing parents to decide who can contact the account, and which groups the account can join; screening message requests from unknown contacts; and managing its privacy settings, with all changes protected by a PIN set by the parent.

About a few weeks later, WhatsApp further expanded this feature on iOS by adding a dedicated "Parental Supervision" section within the "Settings" app, making it easier for parents to find and configure managed accounts.

Today, WhatsApp is again extending these supervision features — this time extending parental monitoring from children under thirteen to teenagers, while giving parents clearer insight into their children's group activity, greater say over how teenagers use "Channels" and status updates, as well as their use of Meta AI, the latter of which may be even more important.

With this update, parents can now receive notifications when teenagers join or leave groups, as well as when there is a "significant increase" in the number of members in groups they have already joined. In addition, parents can choose how teenagers use "Channels", whose status updates they can view, and who can view the status updates they post.

As for Meta AI, parents can now choose between the standard experience designed for users aged thirteen and above, and the more restricted "Limited Content" option, depending on what they consider more appropriate for their child.

WhatsApp said the "Limited Content" setting will further restrict the topics teenagers can discuss with Meta AI. Once enabled, Meta AI features that rely on "Private Processing" will also become unavailable.

WhatsApp also emphasised that these parental supervision features do not allow parents to view teenagers' actual messages or call content, as these communications remain protected by end-to-end encryption.
